Through Software Testing classes in Pune at 3RI Technologies, she gained practical testing skills, guidance, and confidence to restart her career and move into Software Testing at XtrazCon. Table of Contents Shrutika Patil September 18, 2026 8:00 pm Supriya Yogesh Yadav’s journey can help you understand how a career change is possible even after a long professional gap and from a completely different educational background. With an MSc in Mathematics and a 15-year career gap , she chose to move into the IT industry and build a new career in software testing. Her experience shows how structured learning, practical exposure, and the right technical training can help make such a transition more manageable. Through the Diploma in Software Testing—Python at 3RI Technologies , Supriya developed her understanding of software testing and gained practical exposure that supported her move into the testing domain. She eventually started her professional journey in Software Testing at XtrazCon. The Challenge Moving from an MSc in Mathematics to software testing after a 15-year career gap was a new challenge for Supriya. She had an analytical academic background but needed to learn the technical skills required to enter the IT industry and understand software testing in a practical way. Choosing the right Software Testing classes in Pune helped her learn testing concepts, get practical exposure, and become familiar with industry-relevant tools. This gave her the right direction to move ahead with her career change into software testing. The Learning Approach at 3RI Technologies After a career break, Supriya wanted to make a fresh start in the IT field . Since she came from a Mathematics background, she was looking for a course that could help her learn software testing step by step. She joined the 4-month Software Testing course at 3RI Technologies , where she learned Manual Testing, Automation Testing, Selenium, Java, TestNG, JIRA, SQL, API Testing, and Performance Testing , along with practical assignments and project work. What made the learning easier for her was the focus on practical training . Instead of only learning concepts from books, she got to work with testing tools and understand how testing is done in real projects. This helped her become more comfortable with the IT field, gain confidence, and take her first steps towards a career in software testing. Are you looking after Career Guidance from Experts? The 5-month Software Testing program at 3RI Technologies covers the following areas through practical learning, assignments, projects, and interview preparation. Weeks 1–4 – Building the Basics: She started with computer and programming basics, operating systems, networking, Linux, and MySQL. This gave her a basic technical foundation before moving into testing. Weeks 5–8 – Understanding Software Testing: The next stage focused on manual testing, SDLC, STLC, functional and non-functional testing, regression, retesting, test cases, and defect management. She also learned how tools like JIRA are used to track and manage bugs. Weeks 9–12 – Java & Automation: Once the testing basics were clear, she moved to Core Java and Selenium . She learned how automation works, how to create test scripts, use different locators, handle web elements, and work with Selenium WebDriver. Weeks 13–16 – Advanced Automation: The training then moved into TestNG, Page Object Model, Maven, Cucumber, Jenkins, and Selenium Grid . These topics helped her understand how automation projects are structured and managed. Weeks 17–20 – API, DevOps & Projects: In the final stage, she explored API testing with Postman, Git, CI/CD, and Jenkins , along with industry-based projects and case studies. Regular assignments and hands-on practice helped her apply what she had learned. For Supriya, changing her career after a gap was a big step. With the right training and guidance from 3RI Technologies , she was able to build her testing skills, prepare for interviews, and finally get placed as a Software Tester at XtrazCon. The Outcome of Software Testing Classes in Pune For Supriya, learning software testing became a way to explore a new professional direction after a long career break. With a 15-year gap behind her, she decided to step into the IT field and started building her knowledge from the basics. Her training at 3RI Technologies gave her opportunities to understand testing practices, work with commonly used tools, and gain practical exposure through exercises and projects. Over time, this learning helped her become more comfortable with the technical side of software testing and prepare for opportunities in the IT industry. Focus During Training Supriya’s Learning Progress Testing Basics Learned how testers check applications, identify issues, and verify expected results Test Cases Practiced preparing test cases and working with different testing scenarios Selenium Basics Developed an understanding of Selenium and the basics of web automation Testing Tool Worked with tools such as JIRA and TestNG as part of her testing practice Project-Based Practice Used practical tasks to understand how testing concepts are applied to applications Technical Skills Became more familiar with testing terminology, processes, and software workflows Career Preparation Received guidance related to resumes, interviews, and preparing for testing roles Supriya did not try to learn everything at the same time. With regular practice, she slowly understood the testing concepts and learned how to use different tools. Practical tasks helped her connect what she learned in class with real testing situations. The project work also gave her useful experience that she could talk about during interviews and while looking for job opportunities.
